title: A short exact sequence ending in a projective module splits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $0\to K\xrightarrow{i}F\xrightarrow{p}P\to0$ a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $R$-modules ($i$ injective, $p$ surjective, $\mathrm{Im}(i)=\mathrm{Ker}(p)$) with $P$ projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then there are $R$-linear maps $s:P\to F$ with $p\circ s=\mathrm{id}_P$ and $r:F\to K$ with $r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective, line 18795), proof of (1) => (2): as $P$ is projective there is $i\in\mathrm{Hom}_R(P,F)$ with $\pi\circ i=\mathrm{id}_P$, so $F\cong\mathrm{Ker}(\pi)\oplus i(P)$ (stated there for $F$ free; the argument uses only the surjection). Also the first sentence of the proof of Lemma Tag 00O5. Tag verified in tags/tags: 05CF,algebra-lemma-characterize-projective
